answers.answer: Rule is determined by comparing each player's total warriors plus buildings in the clearing. Tokens and pawns do not count. An ordinary tie means nobody rules; the Eyrie rule a tie for most when they have at least one Eyrie piece there. The Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle → Rule (2.5).

answers.answer: A normal move takes a positive number of the player's warriors or pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing, and the player must rule the origin, destination, or both. Rule is rechecked for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle → Move (4.2).

answers.answer: The defender may play one matching ambush (birds are wild); the attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise it deals two immediate hits, not limited by defending warriors, and if no attacking warriors or pawn remain the battle ends. Then resolve before-roll effects, roll (higher die gives attacker hits, lower gives defender hits; ties give equal results), and cap each side's rolled hits by its own warriors in battle. Resolve after-roll effects, then add extra hits (not warrior-capped), subtract ignored hits, and add a defenseless extra hit if the defender has no warriors (for Vagabond, no undamaged swords). Each hit removes an opposing piece; the side taking hits chooses removal order, but must remove all its warriors before its buildings/tokens. Both sides deal their counted hits. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including while defending or outside battle.
answers.evidence: Actions → Battle (4.3), steps 1–6; Scoring / Victory Conditions → 30 VP.

answers.answer: Crafting uses faction crafting pieces matching the card's crafting icons at bottom left, not the card's suit. Each crafting piece can activate only once per turn, except the Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. An item card cannot be crafted unless that item is in the map supply. You cannot craft a persistent effect identical to one already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Actions → Craft (4.1).

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, you may activate a dominance card from your hand, put it in your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of its matching suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Activating dominance is not reversible: the activated card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: A dominance card that would enter the discard pile is instead put near the map as available. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. Bird dominance remains bird, so you must pay a bird card for it; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance card.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: With two players, remove all four dominance cards before shuffling the shared deck; each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins. If the Vagabond is in the game, its setup hides one each of the R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword under the four ruins; without a Vagabond the ruins contain no items. Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. This setup order is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Setup → Standard Setup (Law 5.1), steps 3–7; Vagabond setup (9.3).

answers.answer: Only the Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. If the Keep is removed, it cannot be placed again. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, the Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this also works outside battle. Without a Keep there is no destination for Field Hospitals. The summary does not describe rebuilding the Keep as an exception, and states it cannot be placed again once removed.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) → Keep and Field Hospitals.

answers.answer: In Daylight the Marquise crafts with workshops first, then takes up to three actions plus one additional action per bird card spent outside an action, in any order. A battle is one action. March is one action comprising up to two moves, which may use the same or different warriors; do not interrupt it to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed only once per turn (if supply is short, place the maximum available, choosing eligible recruiters). Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) → Daylight.

answers.answer: To build, choose a clearing the Marquise rules with an open slot and a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost shown atop its column with wood in that clearing or in other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the newly uncovered track space. Building requires the full wood cost, an available building, and a legal slot.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) → Daylight → Build.

answers.answer: Eyrie Birdsong: (1) if its hand is empty, draw one card for Emergency Orders; (2) add one or two hand cards to the Decree, with at most one bird card added; (3) if there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) → Birdsong, in order.

answers.answer: After crafting with roosts, resolve every Decree card by columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within a column the Eyrie chooses the card order. Birds are wild. Recruit places a warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic). Move requires moving at least one warrior from a matching clearing under normal path and rule requirements. Battle initiates a battle in a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build places a roost in a matching clearing the Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no existing roost there. If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason, including lack of pieces, Turmoil begins immediately.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) → Daylight.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except the Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none are face up, flip all leaders face up first); then retuck the Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends and the Eyrie proceeds to Evening. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings. Evening scoring and draw still happen after Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) → Turmoil, in order; Evening.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card, with birds counting; moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, and the Alliance draws one card from the deck into Supporters. The supporter capacity still applies, so incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded. The summary gives the no-card fallback, but does not specify a different payment if the supporter stack is full beyond this capacity rule.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) → Outrage; Supporters capacity.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, the Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt selects a sympathetic clearing with no base matching a base still on its board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit, and places one warrior in the Officers box. It scores normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed; an enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed. Spread Sympathy selects an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if there is no sympathy, and spends the supporter cost shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law if any one other player has at least three warriors there. It places sympathy and scores the uncovered track VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; the Keep's placement ban applies. The summary says Revolt uses two matching supporters and Spread Sympathy uses the listed cost plus any Martial Law supporter; it does not give a separate numeric base cost for each specific token.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) → Birdsong: Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

answers.answer: Train spends a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one Alliance warrior from supply in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay. During Evening, the Alliance may take military operations up to its number of officers, in any order and number: one Move, one Battle, Recruit one warrior at a base, or Organize by removing one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing to place sympathy there and score the uncovered VP. Officers remain on the board when used. When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) → Losing a base; Daylight Train; Evening military operations.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh then. Slip is optional and moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of a clearing. A normal Vagabond move exhausts one boot, plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of a Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in a forest, Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. The Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on its track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) → Birdsong, Daylight Move, Evening.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track, and scores one VP if an item is taken; remove the ruin when its last item is taken. For a Quest, choose a face-up quest matching the clearing and exhaust its two listed items, then complete it and choose either VP equal to the number of matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards; display a replacement quest. No cards pay for a Quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel without changing its face; a ready tea, coin, or bag moves to its track if there is space.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) → Daylight: Explore, Quest, Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a faction that is not already Hostile immediately makes that faction Hostile to the Vagabond, except the special allied battle-loss case. During battle on the Vagabond's own turn, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior whose removal first made that faction Hostile; ordinary building/token removal VP also applies. There is no Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile relationship out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing may it instead remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and scores no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) → Relationships: Hostile/Infamy; Daylight Strike; Aid.

answers.answer: The Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition, choosing a player with the lowest VP among players other than itself (choosing among ties). It places its score marker on that player's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins by dominance. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Vagabond coalition (9.2.8).
